content: Epinephrine administered intranasally can increase the systemic absorption of other nasal products by altering the nasal mucosa for up to two weeks post-administration. This effect necessitates close monitoring when co-administering intranasal epinephrine with other medications. 1. Midazolam (Intranasal): Intranasal epinephrine increases midazolam levels. Cardiovascular Effects: Intranasal epinephrine may cause angina, arrhythmias (including fatal ventricular fibrillation), cerebral hemorrhage, hypertension, pallor, palpitations, tachyarrhythmia, tachycardia, vasoconstriction, ventricular ectopy, and stress cardiomyopathy. Metabolic Effects: Transient hyperglycemia and sweating may occur. Neurological Effects: Disorientation, impaired memory, panic, psychomotor agitation, sleepiness, tingling, and weakness are possible. Psychiatric Effects: Anxiety, apprehensiveness, and restlessness may be observed. Respiratory Effects: Respiratory difficulties may occur. Pregnancy and Lactation: Long-term data on epinephrine use in pregnant women do not indicate a risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Epinephrine transfer into breast milk is expected to be low due to poor oral bioavailability and a short half-life. Treatment for anaphylaxis in breastfeeding patients should not be delayed. Pharmacodynamics: Epinephrine acts as an alphaand beta-adrenergic agonist. Alpha-adrenergic effects reduce vasodilation and vascular permeability during anaphylaxis, preventing intravascular fluid loss and hypotension. Beta-adrenergic effects relax bronchial smooth muscle, alleviating bronchospasm, wheezing, and dyspnea. It also relieves pruritus, urticaria, angioedema, and gastrointestinal/genitourinary symptoms by relaxing smooth muscle in the stomach, intestines, uterus, and bladder. Administration Instructions: Intranasal epinephrine is for single-use only. Do not prime or reuse. Administer using the right hand for the right nostril or the left hand for the left nostril. Insert the nozzle into the nostril until fingers touch the nose, hold the spray straight, and press the plunger firmly. Avoid sniffing during and after administration. If a second dose is needed, administer a new spray into the same nostril after 5 minutes. If more than two doses are required, administer under direct medical supervision. Storage: Store at 68–77°F (20–25°C). Excursions up to 122°F (50°C) are permitted. Do not freeze; frozen solution will not deliver epinephrine effectively.
